content:
# Gospel of Philip — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, pp. 51-86 | Coptic

---

## Chapter 1

**1** One Hebrew produces another Hebrew — and that person is called a "convert." But a convert does not produce a convert. Some people simply are what they are and make others like themselves; others just happen to come into being.

**2** A slave wants nothing but his own freedom. He has no interest in his master's estate. But a son is not merely a son — he expects to inherit his father's whole world.

**3** Those who inherit from the dead are dead themselves, and dead things are all they inherit. Those who inherit from the living are alive themselves — and they inherit both the living and the dead alike.

**4** The dead inherit nothing. What could a dead person possibly inherit? But here is the wonder: if a dead person inherits from someone living, they will not die — they will, against all expectation, begin to live.

**5** The pagan does not die, for the pagan has never truly lived and therefore has nothing to lose. But the one who has believed the truth has come alive — and now faces the real danger of dying, because that person actually lives.

**6** Since Christ came, the world was created, cities were built, and the dead were laid to rest.

**7** When we were Hebrews, we were orphans — we had only a mother. But when we became Christians, we gained both father and mother.

**8** Those who sow in winter harvest in summer. The winter is this world; the summer is the coming age. Let us sow in the world so that we can harvest in the summer. That is why praying in winter is not the right thing to do.

**9** Summer comes out of winter. But anyone who tries to reap in winter will only be pulling things up — not harvesting — because the season produces nothing. [...] Not only [...] in this way [...] but even the Sabbath turns out barren.

**10** Christ came for different reasons: to ransom some, to rescue others, to set still others free. He ransomed strangers and claimed them as his own. He set aside those who were already his — the ones he had pledged, according to his own will.

**11** He did not wait until he appeared among us to lay his life down willingly. He laid it down from the very day the world began. Then he came to reclaim it — because it had been pledged. It had fallen into the hands of thieves and been taken prisoner. But he rescued it. He redeemed both the good and the evil in the world.

**12** Light and darkness, life and death, right and left — they are brothers and sisters of one another. The good cannot simply abandon the evil, nor the evil abandon the good. Life cannot shed death, nor death shed life. In the end, each returns to where it began. But those who have risen above the world — they cannot be dissolved. They are eternal.

**13** The names attached to worldly things are deeply misleading. They pull the heart away from what is real and toward what is not real. When someone hears the word "God," they do not grasp the real thing — only an image of it. The same with "Father," "Son," "Holy Spirit," "life," "light," "resurrection," "the Church" — all of these. People reach for the name and miss the reality, unless they have already come to know the real thing. The names we hear in the world deceive us. If those same words belonged to the higher realm, they would not be mere worldly names. They have their ending in the aeon.

**14** There is a single name never spoken aloud in this world — the name the Father gave the Son. It surpasses every other name. This is what it means to be the Father: the Son could not have become the Father without taking on the Father's name. Those who hold this name know it and do not speak it. Those who do not hold it do not know it.

**15** Truth brought names into the world for our sake. Without names, truth cannot be taught. Truth is one — and yet it is many — and for our sake it teaches the one thing through the many.

**16** The archons wanted to deceive humanity. They saw that human beings were akin to what is truly good. So they took the names of the good and fastened them onto the not-good, hoping to deceive people through the names and lock them to what is not-good. And what an irony: by doing this they did humanity a favor! They caused people to leave behind the free things and seize what is enslaved.

**17** A farmer cannot do his work without [...] water. Similarly, nothing can be built without water and fire [...]. The farmer reaps because of water and earth.

**18** God is a dyer. Good dyes — the kind called "true dyes" — dissolve into the things they dye. The same is true of those whom God has dyed. Because his dyes are deathless, they become deathless through his colors. God dips those he dips in water.

**19** You cannot see anything that truly exists unless you become like it. In this world that is not how it works — a person sees the sun without becoming the sun, sees the sky and the earth and everything else without becoming any of them. But in the realm of truth it is different. You saw something there, and you became it. You saw the Spirit — you became spirit. You saw Christ — you became Christ. You saw the Father — you will become the Father. Here in this world you see everything but do not see yourself. There, you will see yourself — because you will have become what you see.

**20** Faith receives. Love gives. No one can receive without faith. No one can give without love. So to truly receive, we believe. And to truly give — because those who give nothing have nothing — we love.

**21** Before Christ came, there was no bread in the world. Think of paradise, where Adam was: many trees, food for animals, but no wheat for human beings. Adam ate like an animal. But then Christ, the complete human, came and brought bread down from heaven so that humanity could be fed with human food.

**22** The archons imagined they were acting by their own power and will. But the Holy Spirit was secretly accomplishing everything through them, working its own will.

**23** Truth has been sown everywhere since the beginning. Many see the sowing. Few see the harvest.

**24** Some people say, "Mary became pregnant by the Holy Spirit." They are wrong. They do not know what they are saying. When has a woman ever been conceived by a woman? Mary is the virgin whom no power defiled. She is a great anathema to the Hebrew apostles and the apostolic men. This virgin whom no power defiled [...] the powers defile themselves.

**25** The Lord would not have said "My Father who is in heaven" if he had not had another father. He would simply have said "My Father."

**26** The Lord said to the disciples [...]: "Go into every house and bring what belongs to you. Bring what is the Father's — but take nothing, carry nothing away."

**27** "Jesus" is a hidden name. "Christ" is a revealed name. "Jesus" does not exist in any other language — it is always "Jesus" wherever he is called by name. But "Christ" in Syriac and Greek is also "Messiah" in every other tongue. "The Nazarene" is the revealed form of what is hidden.

**28** Baptism is "the holy" — it is the highest. Redemption is "the holy of holies." The bridal chamber is holiest of all — the innermost sanctum.

**29** Baptism contains resurrection and redemption; the redemption lives in the bridal chamber. But the bridal chamber is within something greater than [...]. You will not find [...] there.

**30** Those who pray for Jerusalem love Jerusalem. Jerusalem is the vision of peace. Jerusalem gazes upon Jerusalem. The righteous ones love Jerusalem.

**31** Those who are holy in the fullest sense shall be fed by truth. [...] Some of them [...] the animals [...].

**32** In this world those who wear garments are greater than the garments. In the kingdom of heaven, the garments are greater than those who wear them.

**33** The whole of existence will be cleansed through water and fire — the visible through what is visible, and the hidden through what is hidden. Some things are hidden inside visible things. There is water within water; there is fire within the chrism.

**34** Jesus approached everyone by stealth. He did not reveal himself as he truly was — he revealed himself in whatever form they were capable of seeing him. He showed himself to all: to the great, as something great; to the small, as something small; to angels as an angel, and to people as a person. For this reason his Word remained hidden from everyone. Some who looked at him thought they were seeing themselves. But when he appeared to his disciples in glory on the mountain, he was not small — he had become great. And he made the disciples great so that they could see him in his greatness.

**35** On that day, in the eucharistic prayer, he said: "You who have joined the perfect light with the Holy Spirit — unite us with the angels as well." Do not despise the lamb, for without the lamb you cannot see the king.

**36** No one comes before the king while naked. The heavenly person must be clothed — and that clothing is light.

**37** Water and fire and light and the Holy Spirit — these are four powers. The complete person uses all of them: for purification and for bringing things to life. The [...] of the bridal chamber [...] by fire and light.

**38** The Holy Spirit breathes through everyone. The powers [...] those in their grip [...].

**39** The archons do not know where the truly wise person comes from — because he does not want them to know, lest they interfere. But will he not reveal himself when he is seen?

**40** The cup of prayer holds wine and water. It is a sign of the blood for which we give thanks. It is filled with the Holy Spirit, and it belongs entirely to the complete person. When we drink from it, we receive the complete person.

**41** The living water is a body. We are meant to clothe ourselves in the living person. When someone comes down to be baptized, they strip themselves and say: "I am going down so that I can receive."

**42** A horse is born of a horse; a human is born of a human; a god brings forth a god. The bridegroom and the bride — so it is. [...] No Jew [...] from a Jew is born a Jew. Such is Christian descent.

**43** Those who say "First I will die, and then I will rise" — they are wrong. If they do not receive the resurrection while they are still alive, they will receive nothing after death. They say the same thing about baptism: "Baptism is a great thing — whoever receives it will live."

**44** Philip the apostle said: "Joseph the carpenter planted a garden because he needed timber for his trade. He made the cross from the very trees he had planted. His own flesh and blood hung from what he had planted. That flesh and blood was Jesus, and the planting was the cross. But the tree of life is at the center of the garden, and from the olive tree came the chrism, and from the chrism came the resurrection."

**45** This world feeds on corpses. Everything that gets eaten here is dead. But truth feeds on life. So no one who is nourished by truth will die. Jesus came from that other place and brought food. He gave life to those who wanted it so they would not die.

**46** God planted a garden. A man lived in the garden [...] not many trees [...] but there was an abundance of trees, and neither animal food nor the fruit of [...] what [...] I desired. But I [...] what they wished [...] This was the garden of God [...] and it gives life.

**47** I ate from [...] that place [...] a man of God [...] killed animals [...]. He prepared meat there. But when he prepared the meat [...] he fed the animals [...] but left the people with nothing. [...] God [...] people [...].

**48** God's desire was that people should eat and animals should not. But when Adam ate, the animals ate too. Eating from the tree — the tree of knowledge of good and evil — they brought death upon themselves and upon the animals.

**49** The Eucharist is Jesus. In Hebrew he is called Pharisath — which means "the one spread out" — because Jesus came to crucify the world.

**50** The Lord entered the dye shop of Levi. He picked up seventy-two colors and threw them all into the vat. He pulled them all out white. "This," he said, "is how the Son of Man has come — as a dyer."

**51** The Wisdom they call "barren" — she is the mother of the angels. And the companion of the Savior is Mary Magdalene. [...] loved her more than all the disciples and used to kiss her often on the [...]. The rest of the disciples were troubled by this and questioned it openly. They said: "Why do you love her more than you love any of us?" The Savior answered: "Why don't I love you the way I love her? When someone blind and someone sighted are both standing in the dark, there is no difference between them. But when the light comes, the sighted person sees the light — and the blind one stays in the dark."

**52** The Lord said: "Blessed is the one who existed before coming into being. For whoever is, was, and shall be."

**53** Human superiority is not something you can see — it lies in what is hidden. That is how a person can rule over animals that are physically stronger, whether in what is seen or unseen. That hidden quality is what keeps people alive. But when a person separates from that quality, the animals kill, bite, and eat.

**54** Nothing great can emerge unless something small comes first. Nothing holy can exist unless something visible comes first. What is hidden would simply dissolve if not for the interplay of what is visible and what is hidden.

**55** Water within water, fire within fire, light within light. That is the baptism of truth.

**56** The Lord performed everything as a mystery: a baptism, a chrism, a Eucharist, a redemption, a bridal chamber.

**57** He said: "I came to make what is below like what is above, and what is outside like what is inside. I came to bring them together in that one place." [...] He makes himself known through types and images.

**58** Those who claim there is a heavenly person and someone above even that person are mistaken. That heavenly person is called "the one below," and the one who holds the hidden things is above him. It is better to say "the inner and the outer," and "what lies outside the outer." This is why the Lord called outer darkness "destruction" — there is nothing beyond it.

**59** He said: "My Father who is in secret — go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret." The one who is inside everything is the fullness. Nothing is more inward than he. This is what they call "the highest."

**60** Before Christ, some people came from a place they would never enter again, and went to a place they would never leave. But then Christ came. Those who had gone in, he brought out. Those who had gone out, he brought back in.

**61** When Eve was still inside Adam, death did not exist. When she separated from him, death entered the world. If she enters into him again and he receives her into himself, death will be no more.

**62** "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me, O Lord?" He said this on the cross. For he had been cut off from that place.

**63** The Lord rose from the dead. He became as he had been — but now his body was a perfected body of flesh. Our own flesh is imperfect. But his flesh is [...] the true flesh.

**64** Truth did not come into the world undressed — it came clothed in types and images. That is the only way the world can take it in. There is a rebirth and there is the image of rebirth — you have to be born again through the image. There is a resurrection and it has its image — the resurrection must arise through its image. The bridal chamber has its image — you have to enter truth through the image. This is what restoration means.

**65** Those who have received it need not only to receive the resurrection but the Holy Spirit as well. "Father" and "Son" are simple names; "Holy Spirit" is a double name. For they are present everywhere — above and below, in what is hidden and in what is open. The Holy Spirit shows itself below, in the hidden realm above.

**66** The Holy Spirit is holy in holy people. The evil spirit breathes low, in the hidden realm. The wise, the good, the holy — they seek their power from above. They may be seen, but they are not rattled. They are not drawn away by either the lower powers or the higher, when they choose to be free.

**67** The fear that lives in a person does not fear a beast that is bigger than it — to the bigger beast it assigns intelligence or beauty or [...].

**68** A slave only wants his freedom — he has no interest in what his master owns. But the son, the real heir, does not just have the right to the father's inheritance — he lays claim to it for himself.

**69** Those who inherit from the dead are dead themselves and inherit dead things. Those who inherit from the living are alive themselves — and inherit both the living and the dead.

**70** Dead people inherit nothing. What could a dead person inherit? But when a dead person inherits from a living one, they do not die — on the contrary, they become even more alive.

**71** The pagan does not die, for the pagan has never lived in the first place. But the believer — the one who has trusted the truth — has truly lived, and now faces the real possibility of dying. Because this person is alive.

**72** Since Christ came, the world has been formed, cities have been established, and the dead have been carried out.

**73** When I was young I was raised among the great. [...] It is a good thing to be raised among the great. [...] When it comes to the Father's estate, a minor will not receive the inheritance. The master of the estate would not hand it over until the child was old enough.

**74** It is the same with the son: the son must not remain merely a son — he must become the father.

**75** Those who receive the chrism are called "anointed." The Father, the Son, the Holy Spirit — it would be wrong to call the Father "Christ" or the Son "Christ" or the Holy Spirit "Christ." None of them owns that name. The name belongs only to the one the Father anoints.

**76** [...] The Father's name is the Son. He did not hide it — it was always there. But the Son himself had no name before the Father gave it to him. The name, once revealed, is none other than the Father.

**77** The Lord's Word said to the disciples: "Eat my flesh and drink my blood." Anyone who says that turns the whole world upside down. The flesh is the Word; the blood is the Holy Spirit. Whoever receives these has food, drink, and clothing all at once.

**78** I take issue with those who insist the flesh will not rise. Then they are doubly wrong. You say the flesh will not rise — fine, then tell me what will, and I will respect you for it. You say the spirit in the flesh? You say the light in the flesh? But even the Word is flesh. The Word became flesh — and it was through that flesh that the Word rose, and everything was reunited through the flesh and the Word.

**79** This resurrection does not belong to the bare soul alone. What rises? Flesh together with soul together with spirit.

**80** The soul and the spirit came into being through water and fire and light — the child of the bridal chamber — through water, fire, and light.

**81** Fire is the chrism. Light is that fire. I am not talking about fire that has no shape — but about that other fire whose form is white and whose light is beautiful, and which gives beauty wherever it shines.

**82** Truth does not come into the world unclothed — it comes in types and images. It cannot be received any other way. There is a resurrection, and there is an image of the resurrection. One must truly be reborn through the image. What is the resurrection? The image must arise through the image. The bridal chamber and its image: one must enter truth through the image — this is restoration.

**83** It is right for those who have received [...] not only to receive redemption but to go inside. [...] Those who receive are brought together through the Word and they receive [...].

**84** Is it not right to pray both night and day? And the one who receives the light [...] does not pray by day — that person is the light. The one who has received the Word [...] does not receive it as a gift. That person [...].

**85** If you are [...] before the days and say [...], all who believe in him [...].

**86** The light begins as a model for those in this world. It was not great at first. But when it grew complete, it became great — and gave to both the world and to the age.

**87** Those clothed in the perfect light — the powers and the angels cannot see their nakedness and cannot hold them down. But this light is put on in mystery, in the union of the bridal chamber.

**88** If the woman had not separated from the man, she would not have died alongside him. That separation was how death began. This is why Christ came: to repair the original separation, to reunite the two; and to those who had died in the separation, to give new life and reunite them.

**89** In the bridal chamber, the woman is united with her husband. Those who have been united in the bridal chamber will not be separated from each other again. That is why Eve separated from Adam — because she was never united with him in the bridal chamber.

**90** Adam's soul came into being through a breath. His partner was given to him from the Spirit — who is [...] his mother. His soul was given to him. [...] But the soul that was given to him — this is the one that [...].

**91** The Word brought forth what it desired — and all that it produced, it produced in secret. But the bridal chamber produces out in the open. On the day of the bridal chamber, nothing is hidden. None of those who share in the bridegroom's celebration are hidden.

**92** Abraham [...] was circumcised, to teach us that it is fitting to cut away the flesh of the world.

**93** As long as someone's inner organs are hidden, the body lives and functions. If those organs are exposed and come out, the body dies. It is the same with the root of evil: hidden, it is strong. Once recognized, it is broken. Once exposed, it dies. This is why the Word says: "Already the axe is laid at the root of the trees."

**94** Cutting alone does not work — what is cut grows back. But the axe digs until it pulls up the root. Jesus pulled up the root of the entire realm, while others had only managed a partial job. For us — let each of us dig up our own root of evil and pull it from our hearts. When we recognize it, it will be uprooted.

**95** But if we do not recognize it, it takes root inside us and bears fruit in our hearts. It rules us. We become its slaves. It takes us prisoner, making us do what we do not want to do, and keeping us from what we want. It is powerful only because we have not seen it for what it is. As long as it exists, it is at work.

**96** Ignorance is the mother of all evils. Ignorance leads to death. Those who come out of ignorance — they did not exist, do not exist, and will not exist. [...] When truth comes, all of this will be made whole.

**97** When truth comes, the things that are complete will be revealed, the hidden things brought to light, and the holy things announced. Truth will show what is hidden. It will call the chosen by name, and the Father will give them what has been prepared for them.

**98** Those who have something — even that will be taken from them. Those who have nothing — even that will be taken. This is the justice of the world.

**99** The Master of the universe is not merely a lord — he is the Father. A "master" has no son, but a father does. We call him "master" only because we have not yet come to know him.

**100** The Word said: "Ask and you will receive; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened." Let us ask so that we may receive. Let us knock at the gate of the treasury of the wedding feast.

**101** When we pray for the Holy Spirit both night and day, we give thanks [...].

**102** The Son of Man came from above. He said [...]. He made himself low — all the way to death. When he died and rose again, those who [...] came to know him. And so it became possible for the complete ones to be revealed in the darkness.

**103** The truly holy person is holy all the way through, body included. If they receive bread, they make it holy. If they receive a cup, or anything else — they purify it.

**104** How then could they not purify their own body?

**105** Jesus completed the water of baptism — and in doing so, drove out death. That is why we go down into the water but not into death, so we are not poured out into the spirit of this world.

**106** When a cold wind blows, winter comes. When the Holy Spirit breathes, summer arrives.

**107** The one who knows truth is free. And the free person does not sin, for "the one who sins is a slave to sin." Truth is the mother; knowledge is the father. The world calls those who appear to be beyond sinning "free." But knowing the truth just puffs them up — it makes them feel free without making them truly aware of their own hearts.

**108** Love builds up. Whoever has been set free through knowledge becomes a servant out of love — for the sake of those who have not yet grasped that freedom. Knowledge is what makes them capable of becoming free.

**109** Love never says "this is mine" — and yet [...] everything belongs to love. Love does not say "this is mine" or "that is mine" but "all of it is yours."

**110** Spiritual love is like wine and perfume. Those who anoint themselves with it enjoy it. While the anointed ones are present, those nearby catch the fragrance too. If the anointed ones leave, those who stayed behind — without the anointing — are left with a bad smell. The Samaritan gave the wounded man nothing except wine and oil — which is to say, nothing but the chrism. And that is what healed the wounds.

**111** "Love covers a multitude of sins." Not so: love does not cover sins at all. What love does is make them invisible.

**112** The light that was joined with the darkness — it did not come out of the darkness. But now it shines in both the darkness and the light. The perfect light will shine everywhere. That is what happens when something becomes complete: it comes into full being.

**113** Say "I am a Jew" — nobody flinches. Say "I am a Roman" — nobody cares. Say "I am a Greek, a barbarian, a slave, a free person" — nobody is troubled. But say "I am a Christian" — and the [...] will tremble. I wish I could receive [...] this name, which [...].

**114** God is a devourer of human beings. And so people are sacrificed to him. Before humanity was sacrificed, animals were being offered. But those they were offered to were not gods.

**115** Both glass vessels and clay vessels are made by fire. But when a glass vessel breaks, it can be remade — it was formed by breath. When a clay vessel breaks, it is destroyed — it was formed without breath.

**116** A donkey walking a millstone traveled a hundred miles. When it was freed, it found itself exactly where it started. Some people travel great distances but have nowhere to go. Evening came and they found — no city, no village, no creation, no nature, no power, no angel. The poor wretches had worked for nothing.

**117** The Eucharist is Jesus. In Hebrew he is called Pharisath — "the one spread out" — for Jesus came to crucify the world.

**118** The Lord walked into the dye shop of Levi. He grabbed seventy-two colors and threw them into the vat. He pulled them all out white. He said: "That is how the Son of Man has come — as a dyer."

**119** The Wisdom called "barren" is the mother of the angels. The companion of the Savior is Mary Magdalene. The Savior loved her more than any of the other disciples and used to kiss her often on the [...]. The rest of the disciples were deeply offended. "Why," they demanded, "do you love her more than you love us?" The Savior looked at them and said: "Why do I not love you the same way I love her? When a blind person and a sighted person are standing together in darkness — there is no difference between them. But when the light comes, the one who can see will see it, and the one who is blind will stay in the dark."

**120** The Lord said: "Blessed is the one who existed before coming into being. For whoever is, was, and shall be."

**121** Human superiority is invisible — it is hidden. This is why we can master animals that are physically stronger, whether in what can be seen or what lies beneath the surface. That hidden quality is what keeps us alive. But when a person breaks away from it, the animals kill, bite, and eat.

**122** The one who knows truth is free. The free person does not sin. "The sinner is the slave of sin." Truth is the mother; knowledge is the father.

**123** Those who are simply prevented from sinning get called "free" by the world. But the knowledge of truth only swells their hearts — makes them arrogant. That, too, is a kind of freedom.

**124** The bridal chamber is not for animals, not for slaves, not for women who have been defiled — it is for free men and virgins.

**125** Through the Holy Spirit we are born again — and through Christ we are born twice. We are anointed by the Spirit. In that birth, we were made whole.

**126** No one can see the bridal chamber without becoming a child of the bridal chamber. A Nazarene — meaning "the one who reveals what is hidden." The son must be born; there is no other way. And the [...] must come.

**127** The holy person is holy down to the very body. If they receive bread, they sanctify it. If they receive a cup, or anything at all — they purify it. And of course they purify the body itself.

---

**Translator's Notes (PNEUMA):**
- The meditative, looping quality of the Gospel of Philip — its tendency to circle back to the same themes (light/dark, the bridal chamber, truth and names) — has been rendered with an emphasis on immediacy and accessible rhythm, while keeping the enigmatic quality intact.
- The text repeatedly shifts between third-person reflection and direct second-person address ("you saw," "you became"), which mirrors a liturgical or initiatory context. This dynamic quality is preserved.
- Verses 51 and 119, and 50 and 118, are near-duplicate passages. Both are retained as the text preserves them — the repetition is intentional, reflecting the anthology's compositional texture.
- The passage on Mary Magdalene (vv. 51, 119) contains a genuine manuscript gap (lacuna) at the crucial moment. "Used to kiss her often on the [...]" is the most the text offers. Any stronger rendering imports what the Coptic does not say.
- The bridal chamber (nymphon) consistently refers to a spiritual mystery — the inner sanctum of union — not a physical ceremony. The nymphon is both the highest of the five sacraments and the eschatological goal.
- "Pharisath" in vv. 49 and 117: the etymology offered in the text is of uncertain philological validity and appears to be a creative theological etymology rather than a strict linguistic derivation.

---
